clue.text: Accountant's girl destined to be disbelieved?

definitions.note: a noun in the answer: one whose warnings are fated to go unheeded

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so the possessive gives CA'S
Sandra is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An accountant's girlfriend seems fated never to be believed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess, was cursed to foretell truly and never be believed; the question mark flags the definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Trojan princess was a prophet cursed so that nobody ever trusted her true predictions.

clue.text: Like little birds, cheerful about innards of grub

indicators.note: the cheerful word wraps around the inner letters

parts.note: chirpy means cheerful

indicators.note: innards are the inside, so the middle letters of grub

explanation.surface: Cheerful chicks peck around for bits of grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like little birds' reads as a simile in the surface, but it is the definition: chirruping is the twittering sound small birds make.
explanation.definitionFit: Small birds chirrup, so their twittering manner is described this way.

clue.text: Force that spied best, as intelligence reveals

indicators.note: the phrase reveals the name hidden across its words

explanation.surface: A spying force does best, as intelligence shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stasi was East Germany's secret police.
explanation.definitionFit: East Germany's secret police force spied extensively on its own citizens.

clue.text: Take choir out to get something to eat

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Take the choir out for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thistle-like vegetable whose fleshy heart and leaves are eaten.

clue.text: Taj Mahal's location included in stupid plan

indicators.note: the city is placed inside the word for stupid

parts.note: dim means stupid
the Taj Mahal stands in Agra, India

explanation.surface: A stupid plan includes a trip to the Taj Mahal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing or scheme showing how parts fit is a plan.

clue.text: Endless disturbances holding up a sale

indicators.note: in a down clue the disturbances sit below and support the A
endless means the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: ructions are rows or disturbances

explanation.surface: Constant disruption delays a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims RUCTIONS to UCTION, which in this down clue holds up A above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: A Greek's triumphant cry about old record

indicators.note: the cry goes around the record, holding it in its middle

parts.note: aha is a cry of triumphant discovery
LP, long-playing record, an old vinyl format

explanation.surface: A Greek shouts in triumph about an old record.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet; 'Greek's' reads as Greek is, with the 's a link.

clue.text: He wrote a short work about French art

indicators.note: the A and short work go about the French, around it

parts.note: op. is short for opus, a work
es is French for 'art', as in tu es, you are

explanation.surface: A writer produces a brief piece about French art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is the old English 'thou art': in French, 'tu es' gives ES, a rare device that even seasoned solvers found hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist is a famous writer, so he wrote.

clue.text: Take turn on foot, good way round regular parts of beat

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: the way goes round the picked letters

parts.note: a route is a way

indicators.note: regular means every other letter of beat

explanation.surface: A dancer turns on one foot, beating good time round the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, from pious, is a crossword staple for 'good'; the definition is a ballet movement, a full spin on one foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet spin on one foot is to take a turn on the toes.

clue.text: Law Lord appearing in drink advert

indicators.note: the lord appears inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
lud, as in 'm'lud', addresses a judge

explanation.surface: A judge appears in a drinks advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advert' is the verb, to refer, not an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to refer to it, as one does when hinting.

clue.text: Improper appeal involving tipster's choice

indicators.note: the appeal wraps around the choice, enclosing it

parts.note: IT is sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'
a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection of the day

explanation.surface: An improper appeal involves a racing tipster's pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or inappropriate behaviour can be called improper, a close synonym.

clue.text: Coming down the tree, like voices prophesying war?

definitions.meaning: inherited down the family tree, from forebears
Coleridge's Kubla Khan hears these voices from his forebears prophesying war

explanation.definitionFit: Inherited from forebears down a family tree, and the epithet Coleridge gives the voices in Kubla Khan.

clue.text: Coach pass daughter's lost

indicators.note: the daughter is gone from the pass, taken out of it

parts.note: a railcard is a British discount pass for train travel
D is the abbreviation for daughter; 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A coach pass has gone missing, along with a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAILCARD is a British rail discount card; 'Coach' looks like a bus but is a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled railway carriage is a kind of coach on the rails.

clue.text: Appropriate words identifying Ezra

parts.note: a self-identification, as in saying 'I'm ...'
Ezra Pound, the American poet

explanation.surface: Fitting words to identify the poet Ezra.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra Pound introducing himself would say "I'm Pound"; 'Appropriate' is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize goods or property legally is to appropriate them, the verb sense.

clue.text: Carrying on Tatum's field of activity?

parts.note: carrying on a task is performing it
Art Tatum was a jazz pianist, so Tatum's gives ART'S

explanation.surface: Asking what jazz pianist Art Tatum's line of work was.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Tatum was an American jazz pianist; his given name with the possessive supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama, music and dance together form a broad field of creative activity.

clue.text: Level-headed about girl's nerve affliction

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Ali is a girl's name; the possessive gives ALI'S
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Sensible about a girl's nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical and sensible people are level-headed, seeing things as they are.

clue.text: Speaker on box, possibly, runs after female cat

indicators.note: the runs come after the female and the cat

parts.note: Ann is a female name
an ounce is a snow leopard
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A possible TV speaker chases a female cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is the television; an OUNCE is the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: One who introduces programmes on television, the box, speaks to viewers.

clue.text: Curtail gag about decapitated sailor

indicators.note: the gag goes about the sailor, around it

parts.note: to retch is to gag

indicators.note: decapitated means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a Wren is a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: Retching about a beheaded sailor cuts things short.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, the British women's navy, so counts as a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut back on spending is to curtail it.

clue.text: Be like Casanova — suffer from impaired vision?

definitions.meaning: to be a womaniser always eyeing others
read literally, an eye that wanders out of line

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a flirt eyeing other people, read literally as a wandering, misaligned eye.

clue.text: Harmonious relationship produced by music and wine

parts.note: rap is a style of music
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Music and wine make for a good relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A close, harmonious understanding between people.

clue.text: Exam's length overwhelming woman composer

indicators.note: in a down clue the exam and length sit above the woman

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination; 's is a link
Di is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An exam's length overwhelms a woman composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Little upset encountered in set for play

indicators.note: the little word is encountered inside the set

parts.note: to lay is to set, as a table

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: wee means little

explanation.surface: A small upset is met with in a set for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a stage drama but means slack or room to move, which is why solvers struggled to find the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to move freely, as in a rope with some play in it.

clue.text: Part of fruit, mince pie and fish

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up, so the word pie is cut and rearranged

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A mince pie with fish is part of a fruity recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince pie' reads as a Christmas pastry, but 'mince' is the anagram signal turning PIE into EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer skin of a fruit, botanically the outermost layer of the pericarp.

clue.text: Ticket priest returned, concealing pained expression

indicators.note: the priest's letters hide the cry inside them
returned means the word for priest is turned around

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a priest
ouch is what one says in pain

explanation.surface: A priest returns a ticket while hiding his pained look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns REV into VER, which then conceals OUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A token or coupon exchangeable for goods acts as a ticket.

clue.text: Talk foolishly, being with possessions?

definitions.meaning: to blather or babble, a Scots verb
one who has things, an owner

explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish verb meaning to babble, and jokingly one who has possessions.

clue.text: In art we represented filthy-sounding birds

indicators.note: art and we are represented in a new order
the word for filthy is said, giving a soundalike

parts.note: foul means filthy

explanation.surface: Birds appear in art we have depicted as dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges ART WE into WATER; 'sounding' makes FOUL into its soundalike FOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and other swimming birds are collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Enchanting group try to leave industrial city

indicators.note: the attempt departs, taken out of the city's name

parts.note: Coventry is an industrial city in the English Midlands
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Coventry is an English Midlands city known for car making.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of witches, who cast enchantments, is the classic name for such a group.

clue.text: Fortunate to have new Head in year? It's disgusting

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: fortunate means lucky

explanation.surface: Lucky enough to get a new head teacher this year, yet it's revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new Head' replaces the L of LUCKY with Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish slang for nasty or revolting, exactly what disgusting means.

clue.text: German city's cunning galley captain

parts.note: Trier is a German city on the Moselle; 's is a link
arch means sly or cunning

explanation.surface: A German city is crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the commander of a trireme war galley held this title.
